title: Cloud & Infrastructure
description: Terminos de arquitectura cloud, escalado y fiabilidad para roles senior.

terms.definition: Adding more machines to handle load, instead of a bigger one.
terms.exampleSentence: We handle traffic spikes with horizontal scaling behind a load balancer.

terms.definition: A component that spreads requests across several servers.
terms.exampleSentence: The load balancer routes traffic to the healthiest instances.

terms.definition: Switching automatically to a backup when the main system fails.
terms.exampleSentence: The database has automatic failover to a standby replica.

terms.definition: Resources that have been set up and reserved in advance.
terms.exampleSentence: We over-provisioned the cluster to absorb Black Friday traffic.

terms.definition: The ability to grow and shrink resources with demand.
terms.exampleSentence: Cloud elasticity means we only pay for what we actually use.

terms.definition: A part whose failure brings the whole system down.
terms.exampleSentence: The shared cache was a single point of failure, so we clustered it.

terms.definition: When live infrastructure no longer matches its declared config.
terms.exampleSentence: We detect provisioning drift by running Terraform plan on a schedule.

terms.definition: The extra delay when a serverless function starts from scratch.
terms.exampleSentence: We keep functions warm to avoid cold start latency on login.

terms.definition: How much of the system a failure or change can affect.
terms.exampleSentence: Splitting the monolith reduced the blast radius of each deploy.

terms.definition: A server that sits in front of others and forwards client requests to them.
terms.exampleSentence: The reverse proxy handles TLS and routes traffic to the right service.

terms.definition: A network of edge servers that caches content close to users.
terms.exampleSentence: A content delivery network cut image load times across regions.

terms.definition: Automatically adding or removing instances based on load.
terms.exampleSentence: Autoscaling spun up four more workers during the traffic spike.

title: Security & Authentication
description: Terminos de seguridad, autenticacion y proteccion de datos.

terms.definition: Encrypting stored data so it is unreadable if disks are stolen.
terms.exampleSentence: All customer data uses encryption at rest and in transit.

terms.definition: A signed credential that proves identity for a while.
terms.exampleSentence: The access token expires after fifteen minutes for safety.

terms.definition: To clean input so it cannot inject harmful code.
terms.exampleSentence: We sanitize user input to prevent SQL injection.

terms.definition: To replace keys or secrets regularly.
terms.exampleSentence: We rotate the API keys every ninety days automatically.

terms.definition: Reducing a system's attack surface with stricter config.
terms.exampleSentence: Server hardening closed every port we were not using.

terms.definition: Requiring a second proof of identity besides the password.
terms.exampleSentence: We enforce two-factor authentication for all admin accounts.

terms.definition: A record of who did what and when.
terms.exampleSentence: The audit trail showed exactly which service changed the record.

terms.definition: All the points where an attacker could try to get in.
terms.exampleSentence: Removing unused endpoints shrank our attack surface.

terms.definition: An authorized simulated attack to find weaknesses.
terms.exampleSentence: The penetration test found a way to bypass the login rate limit.

terms.definition: An attack that injects malicious scripts into a web page.
terms.exampleSentence: We escape output to prevent cross-site scripting.

terms.definition: Both client and server verify each other with certificates.
terms.exampleSentence: Services talk over mutual TLS so neither side can be impersonated.

title: Advanced Databases & Data
description: Consultas, indices y motores de datos a nivel senior.

terms.definition: The database part that picks the fastest way to run a query.
terms.exampleSentence: The query optimizer ignored our index until we updated the statistics.

terms.definition: An index that already holds every column a query needs.
terms.exampleSentence: A covering index let the query skip the table entirely.

terms.definition: A set of reusable database connections shared by the app.
terms.exampleSentence: Under load the connection pool ran out and requests queued up.

terms.definition: How much one transaction can see another's uncommitted changes.
terms.exampleSentence: We raised the isolation level to stop the phantom reads.

terms.definition: A precomputed, stored result of a query for fast reads.
terms.exampleSentence: We built a materialized view so the dashboard loads instantly.

terms.definition: The field that decides which shard a row goes to.
terms.exampleSentence: Choosing user id as the partition key spread the load evenly.

terms.definition: Wasted space left by deleted or updated rows.
terms.exampleSentence: Table bloat slowed the scans until we ran a vacuum.

terms.definition: To take in and store large amounts of incoming data.
terms.exampleSentence: The pipeline can ingest a million events per minute.

terms.definition: Changing a data schema over time without breaking readers.
terms.exampleSentence: We handle schema evolution by keeping fields optional.

terms.definition: A record of where data came from and how it was transformed.
terms.exampleSentence: Data lineage helped us trace the bad number back to one job.

terms.definition: To duplicate data on purpose to make reads faster.
terms.exampleSentence: We denormalized the feed table to avoid expensive joins.

terms.definition: The most performance-critical code that runs most often.
terms.exampleSentence: We keep allocations off the hot path to reduce latency.

title: Cloud Reliability & SRE
description: Lexico de fiabilidad, SRE y operacion a escala para roles senior/lead.

terms.definition: The amount of downtime a service is allowed before you must slow feature work.
terms.exampleSentence: We paused new releases because we had burned the error budget.

terms.definition: A target for reliability, like 99.9 percent uptime.
terms.exampleSentence: Our service level objective is a p99 latency under three hundred milliseconds.

terms.definition: Repetitive manual work that should be automated.
terms.exampleSentence: We cut toil by automating the certificate renewals.

terms.definition: A step-by-step guide for handling a specific operational task or incident.
terms.exampleSentence: The on-call engineer followed the runbook to fail over the database.

terms.definition: A write-up after an incident explaining causes and fixes.
terms.exampleSentence: The blameless postmortem focused on the process, not the person.

terms.definition: The average time to restore service after a failure.
terms.exampleSentence: Automating failover cut our mean time to recovery in half.

terms.definition: Deliberately injecting failures to test resilience.
terms.exampleSentence: Through chaos engineering we found a hidden dependency on one node.

terms.definition: How full a resource is, such as CPU or memory.
terms.exampleSentence: The alert fired when memory saturation crossed ninety percent.

terms.definition: When too many alerts make engineers stop paying attention.
terms.exampleSentence: We tuned the thresholds to reduce alert fatigue on the team.

terms.definition: Being responsible for responding to incidents during a shift.
terms.exampleSentence: I am on-call this week, so I carry the pager.

terms.definition: To raise an issue to a more senior or specialized person.
terms.exampleSentence: If the database is down for ten minutes, we escalate to the DBA.

terms.definition: To keep essential features working when parts fail.
terms.exampleSentence: The app degrades gracefully to read-only mode during maintenance.

title: Architecture Trade-offs
description: Conceptos avanzados de sistemas distribuidos para justificar decisiones a nivel staff.

terms.definition: The minimum number of nodes that must agree for a write to count.
terms.exampleSentence: The cluster needs a quorum of three nodes to accept writes.

terms.definition: The process of choosing one node to coordinate the others.
terms.exampleSentence: When the primary died, leader election promoted a replica in seconds.

terms.definition: When a cluster splits and two nodes both think they are the leader.
terms.exampleSentence: Fencing prevents split-brain when the network partitions.

terms.definition: The slowest responses, like the p99, that hurt user experience.
terms.exampleSentence: We optimized tail latency because the p99 mattered more than the average.

terms.definition: A log written before applying changes so data survives a crash.
terms.exampleSentence: The write-ahead log lets the database recover after a power loss.

terms.definition: Sending one event to many consumers or writing to many places.
terms.exampleSentence: The notification service has a huge fan-out to every follower.

terms.definition: One shard receiving far more traffic than the others.
terms.exampleSentence: A celebrity account created a hot partition that overloaded one node.

terms.definition: Estimating the resources a system will need as it grows.
terms.exampleSentence: Capacity planning told us we needed two more nodes before the launch.

terms.definition: The number of distinct values in a set, e.g. of a metric label.
terms.exampleSentence: High cardinality tags blew up the cost of our metrics.

terms.definition: A unique token that lets a retried request run only once.
terms.exampleSentence: The client sends an idempotency key so a retry never double-charges.

terms.definition: A quick, rough calculation to size a design.
terms.exampleSentence: A back-of-the-envelope estimate showed we needed about ten gigabytes a day.

title: Technical Leadership
description: Lenguaje ejecutivo para liderar decisiones, prioridades y stakeholders.

terms.definition: A high-level plan of what a team will deliver over time.
terms.exampleSentence: The migration is the top item on next quarter's roadmap.

terms.definition: Uncontrolled growth of a project's requirements.
terms.exampleSentence: We froze the requirements to avoid scope creep before the release.

terms.definition: Extra future work caused by taking shortcuts today.
terms.exampleSentence: We booked a sprint to pay down the technical debt in the auth layer.

terms.definition: Genuine agreement and support from others for a plan.
terms.exampleSentence: I got buy-in from the team before changing the branching strategy.

terms.definition: Weighing the pros and cons of competing options.
terms.exampleSentence: My trade-off analysis compared cost, latency and complexity.

terms.definition: The time and capacity a person or team has for work.
terms.exampleSentence: I don't have the bandwidth to take on the audit this week.

terms.definition: To get people to agree on goals and approach.
terms.exampleSentence: Let's align on the priorities before we split the work.

terms.definition: To remove what is stopping someone from making progress.
terms.exampleSentence: I reviewed the PR quickly to unblock the release.

terms.definition: To point out a possible problem constructively.
terms.exampleSentence: I raised a concern about the timeline being too aggressive.

terms.definition: To formally approve that something is ready.
terms.exampleSentence: Security has to sign off before we go live.
